# Rules: Write-ups that span many areas

**Covers:** Product-readiness, chat-first and adoption waves whose one write-up covers many parts of the app. Each area file lists the ones that touch it under "Also touches this area".

How to use this file: read the contents list, then read only the entries your change touches (each line gives the line number where the full text starts). The rules that apply to every change are in the root `CLAUDE.md`. To add a rule, see "Adding a rule" there.

- **APPROVE ONCE, THEN OFF TO THE RACES: every ask is counted, an approved
  plan runs, runs you start do not stop at 12, and a closing offer is acted
  on unless it is the user's call** (v1.402.0; the user's autonomy goal and
  an audit that found none of their three metrics computable; three builders
  + three reviewers + integrate). MEASURE (part A): every card / question in
  every lane publishes `interrupt.asked` / `interrupt.answered` through
  `core/approvals.InterruptNote` (kind card|question|plan, tool, surface,
  thread/turn ids, args_hash, flags; answered adds decision, `actor`
  app|phone|grant|timeout|bench|stopped, `wait_ms`) — COUNTING ONLY: never a
  default alert, bell row, desktop notice, phone message or audit-timeline
  row, never args or text. `resolve(actor=)`; `settled_actor`. A new chat's
  first-turn card has no thread yet: `InterruptNote(thread_for=)` looks it up
  in the turn logs when it settles. `eval/autonomy.py` is THE definition
  (module docstring): `classify_line` nudge|retry|request|ack (a bare
  "yes/ok" is a nudge only after a reply that ended on a question), tasks
  split at request lines, success, hands-off, and conservative AVOIDABLE rules
  — never a plan approval (it IS the "approve once"), a once-only safety
  card, a denial, a timeout or a grant. `GET /autonomy/metrics?days=` (off the
  loop, bounded, `truncated` said, zeros never a 500) feeds
  `components/autonomy/HandsOffCard.tsx`. The chat's Continue press is kept
  as `continuedPresses`. The bench records `facts.asks` and
  `facts.would_have_asked` (one ask per round per permission kind, Claude
  Code / Codex names mapped through the dialect + parity tables; "not known"
  otherwise) — its pass rate on one prompt is metric 3 for the bench.
  `core/nudges.note_nudge` publishes `autonomy.nudged` for each of the
  system's own nudges (PLAN_RUN, STEP_LIMIT_CONTINUE, ROUNDS_EXTENDED,
  CLOSING_QUESTION), counted apart. PLAN RUNS (part B): Allow on the Build
  plan door ("Allow and run") makes the daemon start the act turn itself when
  the plan turn ends cleanly (`routes/build.run_approved_plan`, hidden
  `PLAN_RUN_TEXT` with `continuation: true`, a take-flag — exactly once; never
  after Deny/error/stop/cut-off/steer/queued or newer message/plan mode back
  on/archive/account wait/night task); a low-trust plan turn starts its act
  turn LOW; `finish_for_turn` treats `PLAN_RUN_TEXT` as a carry-on (it is not
  the user's request). STEPS: `runtime.resolve_max_steps` is the ONE place —
  an attended origin with no budget gets setting `attended_run_steps` (60,
  12–200, live), unattended keep `max_agent_steps` (12), explicit wins; an
  attended run at its limit carries on ONCE inside the SAME run
  (`carries_on_at_step_limit`, `STEP_LIMIT_CARRY_ON_NOTE`, one more budget,
  the repeat breaker spans both, `allowance.carry_on_refusal` checked first;
  a caller-typed budget never carries on); RunResultCard offers Keep going
  (continue with resume; `resume_reason` stamped). Document/browser chat
  turns get ONE more round allotment (`more_rounds`, both lanes) before the
  OUT_OF_ROUNDS end. ASK POLICY (part C): `harness/components.ASK_POLICY`
  ("ask about what the user wants or what counts as done, never how; decide
  the rest and say what you assumed") in the harness "How you work" section
  (act + plan, every dialect; a folder's system_prompt.md replaces it), every
  agent run's prompt (before the planner), `chat_turn.CHAT_ASK_POLICY` on the
  chat Tools seam only when `arms_work()`, and `dialects.ASK_TOOL_RULE` on
  all three question tools. CLOSING OFFER: `harness/closing_offer.
  ends_on_offer` (English, last sentence of the last prose paragraph) → ONE
  `CLOSING_OFFER_NUDGE` in harness turns (both lanes, after the text-tool-call
  nudge, before the finish check, never after it ran or `checked_before`) and
  at the agent runtime's flat final answer; never plain chat, plan mode, low
  trust, < 2 rounds left, a read-only reviewer, a child run (helper, mission
  member, delegate), or twice. An offer to SEND / POST / PUBLISH / COMMIT /
  PUSH / MERGE / DEPLOY / DELETE / PAY / BUY / touch production is the user's
  (`user_owns`) and keeps its question, and the nudge itself says it never
  authorises those; offered work that runs out of steps keeps the run's
  answer (`OFFER_CUT_LEAD`). Same release (a pre-existing gap the review
  found): the browser sidebar's allow-everything switch answered a waiting
  RISK card (payment, password, destructive word) — risk cards live in
  `PanelTurns._floor_offered` and the switch skips them. Goldens: only
  `team_first_off_golden_v1400.json` moved (each dialect's system prompt
  gained exactly "\n\n" + ASK_POLICY). OPEN: a plan run is a person's turn,
  so Emergency stop does not refuse it; Enter still answers the plan door;
  helpers and mission teammates also get 60 + a carry-on; a restart between
  the plan turn's end and the act turn's start loses the plan run; the
  bench's `would_card` re-derives the lane's rule for three tools. Pins:
  `tests/test_{autonomy_metrics,autonomy_metrics_review,plan_runs,
  plan_runs_review,attended_steps,chat_more_rounds,ask_policy,closing_offer,
  panel_switch_skips_risk}_v1402.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/{autonomy-metrics,
  plan-runs,keep-going}-v1402.test.tsx`.

  HELPER-AGENT RECEIPT (2A): `RunResultCard.runEnd` — cancelled = neutral

  model> · local|cloud · <secondsText> · N steps · N tool calls" (the where
  part is TurnReceipt `replyWhere`, only when `on_this_network` is a real

  (`runActivity`, <= 20). `lib/runWords` says tools by EXACT name (raw ids only
  in titles). The hand-off stamp (`lib/agentRun`) gains optional status,
  outcome, stepLimit, provider, model, routeNote, workspacePath, tools (<=
  `STAMP_TOOLS_MAX` 20), agent, onThisNetwork — written by `settleHandOff(msgs,
  session, row, steps, plan, result)` on BOTH finalize paths (the row first,
  the ledger result standing in for status/outcome/provider/model);

- **Every surface tells the truth about an outcome — ONE verdict vocabulary,
  and Emergency stop stops what starts on its own** (v1.351.0, product-
  readiness Wave 1, gaps G01-G15 + G18; lanes 1A-1E + integrate). SCHEDULES:
  `scheduling/run_outcome.py` is the ONE `last_status` vocabulary — `ok |
  needs_you | partial | error | cancelled | skipped | missed | ""`;
  `fire_status(Session.outcome)` maps the ledger verdict (`needs_you` →
  needs_you, `completed_with_failures` → partial), a FAILED run whose ask
  expired is `error` since v1.358.0 (it read `needs_you`; the row now says
  "Failed" like the run's own badge, its reason opens with
  `run_outcome.ASK_EXPIRED_REASON`, and the bell and phone say "could not
  finish"), a scheduled workflow PARKED on the user is `needs_you` and a
  goal iteration the engine refused is `skipped` (v1.358.0; both read "ok"
  before), a failed row reads "The run failed: <plain reason>" (class name in
  the log only), the detail is `plain_sentence`. `FAILED_STATUSES` (error +
  legacy "failed") / `NEEDS_A_LOOK_STATUSES` / `SHORT_STATUSES` are what the
  Status map's Schedules star and `/ui/status-line` `short_schedules` count
  (HomeLine: "N scheduled job(s) need a look · Open" → /schedules, below a
  waiting ask). Its twin is `dashboard/lib/scheduleOutcome.ts`
  (`SHORT_SCHEDULE_STATUSES` pinned EQUAL; words + tone for every value). A
  new status value goes in BOTH. THE BELL (`NotificationBell.tsx`):
  `unattendedDoor(origin)` (schedule/goal/workflow/reflex/comm/autonomy) →
  a failed or short run is an `attention` row (counted on the badge, tab
  title and ONE desktop ping until the bell is opened), a clean one `quiet`;
  `needs_you` reads first, like the schedule row. `BELL_ACTIVITY_TYPES` is
  the one list `GET /audit` replays on mount (comma-separated `type`, ≤ 40;
  every entry carries `type`) since `ij.bell.lastSeen` ("While you were
  away", lib/bellAway). A CHAT parked on the user with no window following
  its turn is listed by `GET /chat/approvals/pending` as `{id:
  "chat:<thread>" | "chat:turn:<turn id>", kind: "chat", thread_id, tool,
  requested_at, mission_id: null, project_id: null}` — NAMES ONLY, never
  args (`durable_turns.waiting_unwatched`, both route branches); the bell
  (`parseChatAsk`, "A chat is waiting for your OK" → /chat?thread=) and the
  desktop watcher (`planAskNotifications`, a toast only with no window)
  read exactly that. EMERGENCY STOP: `Orchestrator.create_session` refuses
  `emergency_stop_covers(origin)` (every `is_unattended_origin` EXCEPT the
  person-started `self_dev` default) with `EmergencyStopOn` (a
  RuntimeError; text `EMERGENCY_STOP_REFUSAL`); `stop_unattended` (blocking,
  off the loop) cancels the live ones from `/autonomy/kill` AND the
  platform's `config.changed` watcher (Settings row, Ctrl K, chat); a due
  schedule records `skipped` with `EMERGENCY_STOP_SKIP` and keeps its link.
  A door that should WAIT reads `emergency_stop_reason(origin)` first: the
  assignment dispatcher HOLDS (never claims → never strikes), the goal
  engine refuses honestly (200 `{ok:false, refused:true}`), the phone's
  one-shot and chat hand-off and a desktop reply into a phone thread say
  the sentence BEFORE any "On it" ack, and `ReflexRouter.execute` asks
  before EVERY action (re-review: a rule's `workflow` and `remote_agent`
  actions create no session, so they ran under the stop, and a `session`
  rule's row read "EmergencyStopOn: …" —
  `tests/test_emergency_stop_rules_v13510.py`); any other route door gets the app's
  409 `{detail, code: "emergency_stop"}` handler, never a 500. A person's
  Continue is NOT refused (`continue_session` builds its row itself —
  pinned). (A manual workflow Run's agent steps were refused here — origin
  `workflow:<name>` cannot tell a person from a trigger — until v1.352.0's
  `started_by_person`; see that bullet.) Known: the TOML
  `[[triggers]]` cron in `workflows/triggers.py` has no live caller. THE
  RECEIPT (G18, for wave 2): `agents/outcome.session_result` always carries
  `provider`, `model` (the served pair), `agent_name` (roster name or None),
  `agent_type`; with `receipt=True` — `GET /sessions/{id}/result` and (v1.352.0) the
  daemon-appended chat line (`chat_delivery.delivery_result`); the
  finalize/coach/compaction callers skip it for cost — also `route_note`
  (the mission screen's failover/refusal sentence, "in this run", else ""),
  `on_this_network` (`egress.stays_on_this_network`, None with no
  provider) and `activity` (≤ `RECEIPT_ACTIVITY_MAX` = 20 newest plain
  lines, oldest first, `{at, who, session_id, text, tone: ok|warn|ask}` —
  `mission.tool_activity`'s words, shared, not copied). `/sessions` rows
  carry `agent_name` + `interrupted_at`. Dashboard types: `RunResult`
  (components/chat/RunResultCard.tsx), `SessionView`, `AuditEntry.type`.
  CHAT LANES (lock-step): G06 — the honesty note skips after any
  `_FILE_CHANGING_TOOLS` / `_may_have_changed_files` tool, and judges a
  CHANGE claim only when the file is what changed; `custom_tools_used(

  orchestrator's two summary sites. G10 — `is_demo_route` → one
  `demo_note()`. G14 — the Environment line is `model_where_line` from

- **Fast where people wait: the turn, the boot, the poll** (v1.311.0, /goal
  adoption wave 3 — 17 speed findings). CHAT LANES (both, lock-step):
  `chat_turn._gather_grounding` runs every independent grounding hop
  CONCURRENTLY off the loop and the lanes join the result in the old fixed
  order (byte-identical prompt, pinned; learning runs on "" because it
  APPENDS; attachments/skill/workspace stay outside; no silent deadline);
  connector toggles are resolved ON the loop (a worker iterating the registry
  raced a pack registering). Auto-compaction finally runs
  (`_compaction_complete` read off `platform` first). A round's tool calls
  go through `_run_tool_round`: every card is answered first, then only the
  allow-list `CONCURRENT_READ_TOOLS` (never browser/desktop/pane tools, never
  a reader that cards, never `_store_as`) runs with `asyncio.gather`, its
  taint applied in call order BEFORE the writers run serially in model order;
  frames and `role=tool` messages keep the original call order. The stream
  lane STREAMS the final-answer nudge and the language rewrite (a new `reset`
  frame clears the bubble; `useChatStream` handles it in both reducers;
  `done.reply` stays authoritative). `GET /chat/threads` is ORDER BY/LIMIT in
  SQL with a `json_valid`-guarded count (`ix_chatthreadrecord_updated_at`).
  `estimate_tokens` is one run-class regex (~60x, byte-identical);
  `fabric.recall` fans its stores out per call, results in submission order.
  BOOT: the daemon builds the platform with `defer_mcp=True` and loads packs
  in the background (CLI callers of `build_platform` keep the synchronous
  contract); a pack reads `state: "starting"` (`/mcp/servers`, the Tools
  badge, the doctor) until it answers; `platform.mcp_ready` is the lifespan's
  event and `mcp.tools.wait_for_starting_packs` makes a chat turn or an agent
  run wait up to `PACKS_TURN_WAIT_S` (10 s) for it, then `packs_starting_note`
  rides `_Grounding.after_skill()` (both lanes) and the runtime prompt —
  scoped to a platform whose OWN load is running (`_LOAD_STATUS` is
  process-wide); the assignment dispatcher waits on the same event; a Retry
  closes the clients of the tools it replaces. CLI presence is memoised with
  stale-while-revalidate (`cli_binary_present`, one background refresh per
  binary, generation-checked); `POST /providers/rescan` calls
  `invalidate_cli_presence()` first so Re-detect really looks again. The event
  bus runs sync handlers in ONE executor hop; outbound webhooks keep an
  in-memory subscription index (invalidated on any ORM write, one entry per
  (type, record)); undo/revert write off the loop; the Build Files panel keeps
  the newest N by mtime. DASHBOARD: `DaemonProvider` keeps /health when
  unchanged and `epoch` lives in `lib/daemonEpoch.ts`; `useApi`/`usePolledApi`
  share `useApiCore` (a poll never flips `loading`, an equal answer sets
  nothing, identical in-flight GETs are joined); `useEvents(n, {types})`
  filters per subscriber (Overview, bell, MoodOrb, notify bridge, downgrade
  banner, chat page). CHAT PAGE: reopening paints the cached thread at once
  WITH its setup and its PROJECT (`followThreadProject(cached)` — a null
  project on the paint untagged the thread), restores the last conversation,
  fetches the list once, and lazy-loads DocPreview/FilesPanel/DirectoryTree/
  EmailComposeDialog (`components/chat/emailDraft.ts` holds the helpers the
  page renders). Measured: /chat first load 283 → 266 kB. Pins:
  `tests/test_wave3_{chat_lanes,chat_helpers,platform_speed,packs_starting}_v1311.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/{hooks-wave3,chat-wave3,chat-wave3-reset,chat-wave3-seeded-race}-v1311.test.tsx`,
  `chat-wave3-deferred-v1311.test.ts`.

- **Wave 1 of the chat-first plan: 17 verified bugs fixed** (v1.433.0;
  docs/CHAT-FIRST-PLAN-2026-11-04.md, approved "as recommended", D1-D7; four
  groups, each built then independently reviewed, 24 more defects found by the
  reviewers, every fix red-then-green and mutation-checked).
  - DEVICE SETTINGS (D1):
    - `lib/deviceSettings.ts` + `components/DeviceSettingsBridge.tsx` (mounted
      once in the layout, `useEvents(10, {types: ["config.changed"]})`) read GET
      /settings/device at load, on reconnect and on a `config.changed` naming a
      `device.*` key.
    - They apply theme (built-in ids only, `applyTheme`), read aloud (every
      useTTS), persona (new chats) and Auto tools (the chat switch).
    - Apply only a value changed since this window last knew it
      (`ij_device_known`). The FIRST sight of a key keeps what the screen already
      shows and PUTs it up once (update day).
    - A save not yet answered owns its key: a read meanwhile skips it and reads
      again. Saves run one at a time, in press order. A refused save puts back
      the daemon's own last value.
    - Screen presses (ThemeSwitcher, Ctrl K "Theme:", ThemeMaker, read aloud,
      persona, Auto tools) PUT the row; a theme you made sets it to null.
    - `device.theme` is an enum pinned to `lib/theme` THEMES: a NEW built-in theme
      needs a schema option. Settings > Appearance has ONE theme control
      (CONTROLLED_IN_SECTION).
    - Never import `lib/deviceSettings` from `__tests__/setup.ts`; reset through
      `deviceSettingsState`.
  - SETTINGS/CONFIG:
    - The writer clears every app's own `auto_approve` on any Off of
      `mcp_auto_approve`. It counts only rows `pack_grants_auto` says opened the key.
    - `active_project_id` is validated in the writer: unknown or archived ids are
      refused in the activate route's words, "" is allowed, and an unchanged value
      is not re-checked.
    - `max_concurrent_children`, `assignments_enabled`, `curator_enabled` and the
      three curator numbers are real Config fields with schema rows. The curator
      loop starts at boot and reads its switch every pass.
    - `event_retention_days` is ask-floor, restart=False.
    - Permission rows: `web_look` allow (READONLY), `pixio` ask, `delegate_remote`
      ask. pixio_models/params are READONLY, but `pixio_status` is NOT: it saves
      files.
  - A CREDENTIAL IS NEVER A TOOL ARGUMENT:
    - Discord's webhook URL comes through the secure card into
      `comm.channels[name].webhook_url` (where the Notifications page reads it). A
      passed `webhook_url` is refused before any card.
    - A Postgres connection string with a password is refused in chat and taken on
      the card into `arg_secrets` (`mcp.postgres.connection`).
    - `records.masked_args` redacts both tools' log rows, versioned Discord paths
      included.
    - The composer's paste guard (lib/configCards SECRET_SHAPES, twinned in
      harness/step_target.py) holds Discord webhooks (with or without https://)
      and postgres/mysql/mariadb/mongodb(+srv)/redis/sqlserver URLs carrying a
      password.

  banner; never driven in the packaged app.

- **Words and lines that differ by system read ONE module name
  (`_ON_WINDOWS`), never `os.name` at the call, so a test reads both
  systems' words on any machine** (v1.518.0). `onboarding/doctor._ON_WINDOWS`
  picks the health check's words: off Windows `check_local_ocr` says scans
  need a model that can read images (never "Settings → Time & language" or
  "winrt"), `check_legacy_office` says save `.doc` as `.docx` (never
  "Install Microsoft Word"), `check_uv` gives the `curl … | sh` line.
  `terminals/ai_clis._ON_WINDOWS` picks the install line: off Windows
  `launch_line` returns the entry's `command_sh` (`curl -fsSL
  https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`, `curl -fsSL
  https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh`; both answered 200 on
  2026-11-16) for every pane; Windows keeps PowerShell, and cmd's form in a
  cmd pane. `doctor._LINUX_EDGE_NAMES` (`microsoft-edge`,
  `microsoft-edge-stable`) and `_LINUX_EDGE_PLACES`
  (`/opt/microsoft/msedge/msedge`) are `()` on Windows; `_browser_label` and
  `page_browser.edge_executable` accept a name that starts `microsoft-edge`.
  A test patches `_ON_WINDOWS` (or the two tuples), NEVER `os.name`:
  `pathlib` then refuses to build a path. The older install-job tests set
  `_ON_WINDOWS = True` so they pin Windows' lines on Linux too. Pins:
  `tests/test_linux_desktop_v1518.py`, `tests/test_cli_install_jobs_v14490.py`.
  The dashboard still has NO fact for "which system is this": the setting's
  label "Start Iron Jarvis with Windows", `%APPDATA%` in Help and the
  signed-out banner, "Windows Firewall" and "Match Windows" are still wrong
  on Linux (the next step: one platform field on /health, read once).
